\section[talesuttu]{\kn{ತಲೆಸುತ್ತು} (talesuttu) — dizziness}

\label{lesson:KA-C93-dizzy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a job, then the Kannada for English.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತಲೆಸುತ್ತು}}
\textbf{\kn{ತಲೆಸುತ್ತು}} (\emph{talesuttu}) — \textquotedblleft{}dizziness\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}head-spinning\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\kn{ತಲೆ}} (\emph{tale}), \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\kn{ಸುತ್ತು}} (\emph{suttu}), \textquotedblleft{}to go round\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ತಲೆಸುತ್ತು}} (\emph{nanage talesuttu}) — \textquotedblleft{}I feel dizzy\textquotedblright{}, built like \textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ತಲೆನೋವು}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Head, and a turn, make one more head word.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{talesuttu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{talesuttu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nanage talesuttu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a job, then the Kannada for English, then say \emph{talesuttu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತಲೆಸುತ್ತು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Dizziness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[seke]{\kn{ಸೆಕೆ} (seke) — sultry heat}

\label{lesson:KA-C93-sultry}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for English, then the Kannada for dizziness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸೆಕೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸೆಕೆ}} (\emph{seke}) — \textquotedblleft{}sultry, sticky heat\textquotedblright{}, the heat that makes you \textbf{\kn{ಬೆವರು}}, \textquotedblleft{}sweat\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ತುಂಬಾ} \kn{ಸೆಕೆ}} (\emph{tumbā seke}) — \textquotedblleft{}it's very hot and sticky\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Heat you can feel on the skin.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{seke}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{seke}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{tumbā seke}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for English, then the Kannada for dizziness, then say \emph{seke} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಸೆಕೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sultry heat\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[ārāma]{\kn{ಆರಾಮ} (ārāma) — ease, comfort}

\label{lesson:KA-C93-ease}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for dizziness, then the Kannada for sultry heat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಆರಾಮ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಆರಾಮ}} (\emph{ārāma}) — \textquotedblleft{}ease, comfort, rest\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ಆರಾಮಾಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ}?} (\emph{ārāmāgiddīrā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}are you well, are you at ease?\textquotedblright{}, a warm way to ask how someone is.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The feeling that comes after rest.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ārāma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ārāma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{ārāmāgiddīrā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for dizziness, then the Kannada for sultry heat, then say \emph{ārāma} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

One more word for the doctor.
